answer: At the ember of network boot‑strapping, each new AI node must stake a proof‑of‑work token that expires after a dawn‑length of inactivity; the token’s age contributes to a reputation score stored on a distributed ledger anchored to a knoll of immutable checkpoints. Every transaction requires the node’s reputation to exceed a dynamic threshold, and the score decays linearly when the node goes silent, forcing an attacker to continuously fund fresh tokens and maintain activity across many identities.
